decision_policy.llm_role: optional narrative only; never decides applicability
decision_policy.unknown_fact_policy: return every application in the selected category as a candidate and ask targeted questions before filing

global_rules.rule: Use the project address to confirm that the work is inside Kansas City, Missouri; Kansas City, Kansas is a different jurisdiction.
A permit application and a plan application are distinct CompassKC records. Work needing formal plan review requires the applicable approved plan before or together with its permit workflow.

Commercial and multifamily trade permits must be obtained by appropriately licensed contractors. A qualifying owner-occupant of a single-family residence may perform eligible work only through the homeowner-affidavit process.
Permit-exempt work does not waive compliance with the adopted codes, zoning rules, utility rules, or other approvals.
When work is connected to an existing plan or building permit, create the trade permit from that record's sub-record tab when CompassKC directs it.

rules: Formal commercial plan review is required when the work is not minor enough for the miscellaneous-renovation permit route.
Fast-track metal-stud work is at risk, is limited to metal studs, requires the IB151 Statement of Understanding, and does not replace full plan approval.
New commercial elevator installations must be linked to an approved building permit; work on existing systems must identify each CVEL number and the exact work.
Commercial plans must include the administrative, architectural, engineering, and special-inspection content applicable under IB110 Parts A-D.
exemptions: Building exemptions listed in the official Building Permit Exempt Work page, including qualifying accessory structures, low retaining walls, low decks/platforms, and qualifying reroof work.
required_documents: construction plans when formal review applies
IB151 Statement of Understanding for fast-track metal studs

rules: Use Electrical General - Commercial for commercial buildings, apartments, and commercial security-alarm installations when plans are already approved or the scope is minor enough not to need full plan review.
Use Electrical General - Residential for detached single-family houses, duplexes, and their detached accessory structures; use Electrical General - Townhouse for IRC townhouses.
Any residential or commercial service of 400 amps or larger requires the completed IB160 submission identified by CompassKC.
Service equipment rated 800 through 1199 amps requires a sealed one-line drawing plan case; for one- and two-family work, the line drawing may be submitted with the permit case as allowed by IB160.
Service equipment rated 1200 amps or more, and every system over 600 volts, requires complete engineered drawings sealed by a Missouri professional engineer.

Transformers, generators, battery systems, fire pumps, wind turbines, and automatic transfer switches require the IB160 plan/line-drawing path; residential generators and home battery systems also require IB160 documentation.
An addition is evaluated using the total resulting electrical service size, not only the added load.
Residential solar must use the Residential Solar Plan application before the associated electrical permit workflow.

Electrical Limited Service - Residential is only for the limited scopes in IB108 and licensed electrical contractors; examples include one new circuit serving no more than two devices, extending circuits to no more than two devices, and hard-wired smoke detectors.
Electrical reconnect permits are inspection-only. They authorize no upgrade, alteration, or new electrical work; discovered work requires a separate licensed electrical permit.
Fire Alarm - Commercial is for minor work not requiring full plans. If plans are required and no building work is involved, file Miscellaneous Trade Work Only Commercial (Includes Fire Alarm).

A hard-wired residential security alarm uses Install Security Alarms - Residential. Wi-Fi and plug-in systems are permit-exempt, but alarm monitoring still requires the separate KCPD monitoring permit.
Floodplain development review may apply to electrical service equipment located in a regulated floodplain.
exemptions: Minor repair and maintenance such as replacing lamps and connecting approved portable plug-in equipment.
Temporary wiring and equipment used only for testing or servicing electrical equipment.
Replacement of snap switches, receptacles, and lighting fixtures when the circuit is not altered; ceiling fans are excluded from this exemption.
Qualifying utility generation, transmission, distribution, metering, and utility-owned equipment.
Wi-Fi and plug-in residential security systems are exempt from the residential security-alarm construction permit.
required_documents: approved parent plan or trade-only plan when required
IB160 and one-line/engineered drawings when triggered

rules: Fast-track sprinkler permits authorize at-risk sprinkler work before full plan approval, require the IB116 Statement of Understanding, and do not replace full sprinkler plan review.
Kitchen hood suppression work requires a fire-protection permit and licensed fire-protection contractor; link it to the building permit when one exists.
Construction or modification of a fire-sprinkler system has a separate commercial plan application in CompassKC.
required_documents: IB116 Statement of Understanding for fast-track work

rules: Select the commercial, residential, or townhouse general application from building type.
Commercial work requires an approved related plan unless the scope is minor enough not to require full plans; trade-only work needing plans uses Miscellaneous Trade Work Only Commercial.
Limited Service - Residential is restricted to the scopes listed in IB108 and licensed mechanical contractors.
Residential air-conditioner and furnace applications are equipment-specific routes.
exemptions: Portable heating, ventilation, cooling and evaporative equipment; replacement parts that do not alter approval; certain self-contained refrigeration systems not exceeding 10 pounds of refrigerant or 1 horsepower; grilles and diffusers; qualifying utility work.

rules: Select the commercial, residential, or townhouse general application from building type.
Commercial work requires an approved related plan unless the scope is minor enough not to require full plans; trade-only work needing plans uses Miscellaneous Trade Work Only Commercial.
Limited Service - Residential is restricted to the scopes listed in IB108 and licensed plumbing contractors.
Gas test/reconnect, residential water heater, and residential-service backflow device are separate application routes.
Private sewage disposal systems follow IB105 in addition to the plumbing permit workflow.
exemptions: Repair of faucets or valves; clearing stoppages; replacement of defective fixtures or valves without piping extension or rearrangement; replacement of sink or lavatory traps; qualifying utility work.
required_documents: backflow or gas-test documentation when applicable

rules: Interior-remodel permits are separated into duplex, single-family, and townhouse routes.
Structural remodels, additions, new dwellings, detached accessory buildings, residential miscellaneous structures, and solar use separate plan applications.
Residential plans must contain the applicable IB100 site, architectural, structural, energy, and administrative information.
Residential swimming pools follow IB119 and the dedicated pool permit route.
Open/uncovered decks have a dedicated permit; qualifying platforms/decks not more than 30 inches above grade and not over a basement or story are exempt.
Residential elevator work has a dedicated permit; exempt devices are limited to the official elevator exemption list.
exemptions: The complete building and elevator exemptions listed on the official Building Permit Exempt Work page.
required_documents: IB100 plan package when plan review applies

rules: Use the exact freestanding/monument, marquee, special-event/temporary, or wall/projecting sign application.
Outdoor advertising signs are subject to IB127 and Chapter 88 location/design rules.
A Council-approved signage plan is a separate plan application when that approval path applies.
exemptions: Copy/message changes; painting and cleaning; signs inside buildings or on vehicles; qualifying wall-painted lettering; municipal, danger and public-service signs; emergency non-advertising signs; and qualifying real-estate signs up to 32 square feet per frontage, as listed by the City.

rules: Commercial and residential work each have complete, interior, partial, and pre-demolition-inspection application routes.
Complete or partial demolition requires the applicable pre-demolition and utility-disconnection steps described by IB107 and the portal.
Historic-resource review is a separate planning record and may be administrative or regular.
Choose the application matching the activity, asset, applicant type, and whether the location is under Parks/Parkways/Boulevards jurisdiction.
Excavation type is separated by utility/purpose; traffic control, street plates, hauling, dumpsters, encroachments, pole attachments, loading, and streetcar access are separate approvals.
The minor-infrastructure permit is remove-and-replace repair only. New driveway entrances require zoning approval; ADA ramps require engineered major-infrastructure review.
Minor infrastructure submittals require the address, detailed scope, quantities, a drawing, and liability-insurance evidence.
Streetcar Track Access applies inside the stated track, overhead-contact-wire, or safety envelope and commonly also requires traffic control.
Public infrastructure work requires separate plan review and permits for the infrastructure disciplines involved.
Major infrastructure includes sanitary sewers, storm sewers, site disturbance, streets/pedestrian facilities, streetlights/signals, and stream buffers.

Site disturbance of one acre or more must be permitted before other infrastructure permits; plans, specifications, calculations, soils/drainage information, and cost estimates must be sealed by a Missouri professional engineer when required by IB159.
Site-disturbance inspections occur at least every 14 days and after qualifying 0.5-inch rain events; the permit remains issued until vegetation is established.
New water service, service-line repair, service kills, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, SAC meters, and water-main transfers are distinct applications.
A water-main transfer requires an approved Water Main Extension plan on file before permit issuance.
Sanitary/storm new or repair work must use its dedicated service-line application; abandonment requires disconnection at the location directed by Water Services.
Water-main extensions and relocations use the separate Water Main Extension-Relocation plan application.
Zoning Clearance for Business License is the operational clearance route for businesses; a Zoning Compliance Letter is an informational parcel record and is not a business-license clearance.
Land-use approvals, development plans, special uses, rezonings, plats, historic review, variances, alternatives, and legal-nonconformance certificates are separate plan applications.
A change of occupancy classification may require both the building plan application and zoning/occupancy approvals.
required_documents: site or development plan when applicable
legal description and notices when applicable

rules: The proposed use and occupancy classification must match the approved building and zoning records before occupancy.
All required building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and fire/life-safety final inspections must be approved before the Certificate of Occupancy is issued.
Outstanding correction notices, permit holds, and required plan revisions must be resolved before occupancy approval.
A change in use or occupancy classification requires the applicable building and zoning review even when the tenant work is limited.
The occupant load, exits, accessibility, restroom facilities, and fire-protection systems must match the approved plans and the actual commercial use.

576.filing_rule: Approved parent plan, or minor scope; otherwise file plan 653.

767.filing_rule: Use parent record sub-record when related.

583.filing_rule: Use parent record sub-record when related.

434.filing_rule: Licensed contractor only; scope must satisfy IB108 limited-service limits.

772.filing_rule: Minor fire-alarm scope only; use plan 653 when plans are required.

432.filing_rule: Hard-wired security alarm only; Wi-Fi/plug-in exempt; separate KCPD monitoring permit applies.

electrical_plan_dependencies.name: Miscellaneous Trade Work Only Commercial (Includes Fire Alarm)

electrical_plan_dependencies.requirement: sealed one-line drawing plan case under IB160
complete engineered drawings sealed by a Missouri professional engineer under IB160

electrical_plan_dependencies.condition: transformer or generator or battery or fire_pump or wind_turbine or automatic_transfer_switch
